_meta.comment: Status: design draft for review - decided, not built. This file is the normative machine shape of the MCP tool catalog declared in mcp-plugin.md: the exact tools/list result payload the plugin serves. The prose catalog and this file describe the same twelve tools (ADR-0025 d12); a divergence between them that pending_design does not list is a documentation bug. tools/list serves the subset of this file the server builds; an entry for a tool the server does not serve yet carries its designed shape, and a served tool's entry describes what the build serves and changes only in the same change as the code that serves it, so the server never advertises a field it refuses. pending_design names, per served tool, what mcp-plugin.md decides that the served entry does not carry yet, or a decided refusal its description states that the build does not raise yet. Target MCP specification revision: 2025-06-18 (streamable HTTP transport, run stateless per mcp-plugin.md); the revision the implementation finally pins, and the transport behavior verified against it, are recorded with a fetch date at implementation time.
_meta.output_shapes: This file declares inputSchemas only. Tool OUTPUT shapes are deliberately prose-normative in mcp-plugin.md until the implementation pins structured output schemas.

pending_design.oml_remember: ADR-0025 d10: the claim_key collision refusal its claim_key description states is decided, not built; the build raises no submission.claim_key_conflict yet.
pending_design.oml_learn: ADR-0025 d10: the claim_key collision refusal its claim_key description states is decided, not built; the build raises no submission.claim_key_conflict yet.
pending_design.oml_recall: ADR-0025 d4, d7, d8, d12, d16: include_own_held and max_tokens inputs; the caller's own held rows among the hits; steering never among the hits; the claim-item output with tokens; the budget object; refusal of unknown and unbuilt fields by name.
pending_design.oml_events_tail: ADR-0025 d15: the scope input (the ring's workarea_id, defaulting to the key's default workarea, request.workarea_unresolved for a key with none); per-family visibility; next_after_seq; the subject and workarea output fields; idle; request.validation for an after_seq beyond head_seq.

tools.name: oml_remember
tools.description: Submit a memory. Held on arrival: scanned same-call, then reviewed by an identity that did not write it, visible to others only after ratification. Success means accepted for review, never published. Rides POST /v1/memories.

workarea.description: Optional target workarea node id. Omitted: the key's journalled default workarea. Present: an override honored only within the key's grants. A path given here is resolved to its node first. A key with neither a default nor a value here is refused (request.workarea_unresolved).

claim_key.description: Groups the versions of one claim; caller-supplied. A new claim collides (submission.claim_key_conflict) only with a held, promoted or demoted version of it in the workarea, and a claim whose every version is rejected or erased releases it.

kind.description: kind: derived_fact is the path for a derived conclusion whose lineage cannot or will not be named (oml_learn requires non-empty derives_from). The vocabulary kinds are ordinary submissions into a vocabulary workarea; ratifying a vocab_release is a human-required verdict under the shipped review policy.

upload_session.description: A completed upload session opened via oml_attach; its recorded digest is bound into the signed submission envelope (D3).

attachments.description: Upload sessions previously completed via oml_attach.

derives_from.description: Artifact ids this memory derives from. Lineage is declared, and the honesty rule applies in full: an omitted derivation is undetectable by the service. Every named ancestor expands the row's reviewer-exclusion set (R2 over the lineage closure).

simulation_id.description: Optional simulation channel id, passed through to POST /v1/memories. Required when derives_from touches a simulation row (submission.simulation_id_required otherwise); writing with it requires the calling key to be in that simulation's journalled audience (simulation.audience_refused).

simulated_time.description: Optional RFC 3339 timestamp, passed through with simulation_id. Declared data, never backdating - the journal keeps the real timestamp.

idempotency_key.description: Scoped to (key, resolved workarea). A retry with the same key and an identical request returns the stored response; the same key with a different request is a typed error, never a second write (D13).

tools.name: oml_recall
tools.description: Search promoted memories within a workarea subtree; steering rows precede hits and are never ranked. Hits are promoted rows only - the caller's own held rows do not appear (use oml_my_work). Every recall is logged to the read log. Rides POST /v1/memories/recall.

query.description: The search text; hybrid FTS + vector is the only search mode.

scope.description: Optional workarea node id. Omitted: the key's default workarea's subtree. Present: one node as an override within the key's grants. Either way the search covers that node's subtree intersected with the key's effective read access.

k.description: How many hits to return, at most 100 as on the ring.

tools.name: oml_learn
tools.description: Submit a derived fact with declared lineage - held on arrival, same admission pipeline as oml_remember. derives_from is the point of the verb: it must be non-empty (submission.lineage_required otherwise); a conclusion without nameable lineage goes through oml_remember with kind derived_fact. Rides POST /v1/memories with verb learn.

workarea.description: Optional target workarea node id, exactly as on oml_remember: omitted, the key's default workarea is the target.

claim_key.description: Groups the versions of one claim. A new claim collides (submission.claim_key_conflict) only with a held, promoted or demoted version of it in the workarea, and a claim whose every version is rejected or erased releases it.

derives_from.description: Artifact ids the conclusion derives from; required and non-empty. A target the key cannot read is refused as unknown (fail closed); a target inside a simulation forces the simulation fence.

simulation_id.description: Optional simulation channel id, exactly as on oml_remember: required when derives_from touches a simulation row, honored only for keys in that simulation's audience.

simulated_time.description: Optional RFC 3339 timestamp, as on oml_remember: declared data, never backdating.

idempotency_key.description: Scoped to (key, resolved workarea), as on oml_remember.

tools.name: oml_get
tools.description: Read one claim version by artifact_id: the calling key's own rows in any state, others' promoted versions within read access. Anything else answers access.not_found. Rides GET /v1/memories/{artifact_id}.

artifact_id.description: The version to read; each version of a claim has its own artifact_id, and superseded versions stay readable as history.

tools.name: oml_supersede
tools.description: Propose a new version of a claim, or with retirement:true propose retiring it. Enters admission held; the old version stays served until a non-author ratifies. Rides POST /v1/memories/{artifact_id}/supersede.

artifact_id.description: The version to replace: the claim's current served tip (submission.tip_conflict otherwise, naming the current tip when the key can read it). A target of a vocabulary kind (term, term_mapping, vocab_release) is refused on this tool with request.validation; supersede it on the HTTP API.

text.description: The new claim text, or, with retirement true, why the claim is retired.

retirement.description: True proposes retiring the claim: once a non-author ratifies, recall stops serving it and every version stays readable by oml_get.

kind.description: Optional successor kind, passed through to the supersede body. With retirement true it must equal the target's kind (request.validation otherwise).

derives_from.description: Further artifact ids the new version derives from; the target is included implicitly. Every id must be readable by the key.

reason.description: Optional reason for the change, passed through to the supersede body.

idempotency_key.description: Scoped to (key, target workarea). A retry with the same key and an identical request returns the stored response; the same key with a different request is a typed error, never a second write (D13).

tools.name: oml_attach
tools.description: Open or inspect a resumable upload session for a file, image or PDF. Chunk bytes do not travel over MCP: parts are PUT to the versioned HTTP API under the same bearer key; this tool opens and inspects sessions, nothing more. Rides /v1/attachments/*.

action.description: open starts a session (requires media_type, size_bytes, expected_digest); status inspects one after a crash or retry (requires upload_session).

media_type.description: With action open: the attachment's media type, recorded and echoed at fetch.

size_bytes.description: With action open: the plaintext size in bytes.

expected_digest.description: With action open: the expected plaintext SHA-256, recorded up front; bytes that do not hash to it at completion never bind (upload.digest_mismatch, session terminal).

upload_session.description: With action status: the session id to inspect; returns state (open | complete | aborted | expired), parts received, and the next part to send.

tools.name: oml_relate_propose
tools.description: Propose a labelled edge - claim-to-claim or workarea-to-workarea. The proposal is journalled and pending; it confers nothing and changes no access until a different dreamer ratifies it (R2 extends to edges). Ratification is not on this surface. Rides POST /v2/claim-edges or POST /v2/workareas/{id}/edges.

kind.description: Which graph the edge lives in; endpoints are workarea node ids or artifact ids accordingly.

label.description: For workarea edges, the closed set: relates_to | continues | derived_from | mirrors. The claim-edge label vocabulary is not fixed by the design - an open detail tracked in the roadmap.

from.description: The from endpoint (workarea node id or artifact id, per kind).

to.description: The to endpoint (workarea node id or artifact id, per kind).

note.description: Optional proposer note, journalled with the proposal.

tools.name: oml_my_work
tools.description: The caller's own submissions and where each stands: held, promoted, demoted, rejected, erased. Scoped to the calling key's own submissions by construction, across every workarea it wrote to, newest first. Rides GET /v1/memories?own=true.

workarea.description: Optional workarea node id, a subtree filter; omitted, every workarea the key wrote to.

claim_key.description: Optional claim_key filter: the versions of one claim.

state.description: Optional state filter. Omit both filters for everything the key wrote, newest first.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page; the client holds it (stateless).

tools.name: oml_workarea_info
tools.description: One workarea as the calling key is allowed to see it: identity, derived path, status, crew record, readable immediate children, and the verbs this key's effective access carries there, with the permission epoch. Rides GET /v2/workareas/{id}, one call.

workarea.description: Optional workarea node id. Omitted: the tool describes the key's default workarea; a key with none is refused (request.workarea_unresolved).

tools.name: oml_graph
tools.description: A scoped read of claims and their edges: declared lineage (derives_from), claim-to-claim connection edges with their pending/ratified state, and supersession chains within a subtree. Serialize, don't compute: closure computation, path finding and ranking are the client's problem. Rides GET /v2/claim-edges and GET /v2/memories/{id}/lineage.

scope.description: Optional workarea node id. Omitted: the key's default workarea.

depth.description: How many hops from the roots; a value above the served ceiling is a typed limit error, never a truncated answer pretending to be whole.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page.

tools.name: oml_events_tail
tools.description: Poll the journalled event stream for the key's scope, from the last journal sequence the client processed. The stateless substitute for push: the server remembers nothing between calls. Gaps in a filtered tail are normal - they are the events this key may not see. Rides GET /v2/events.

after_seq.description: The last per-tenant journal sequence the client processed; events after it are returned, seq ascending. Omit to start from the beginning (0), as on the ring; pass the head_seq of a first call to start from now. A malformed value is a typed request.validation refusal, never a silent restart from zero.

tools.name: oml_vocab
tools.description: Read the tenant's vocabularies: term lookup, deterministic typeahead, hierarchy over the per-release closure, and SSSOM-shaped mappings. One tool, four actions, each one GET /v2/vocab/* call. Strictly read-only at the reader ceiling: proposing a term or mapping is oml_remember with the matching kind, and nothing here deprecates, ratifies or cuts a release.

action.description: suggest takes q (and optionally workarea_id); get and hierarchy take curie; mappings takes term.

q.description: With action suggest: the prefix+label typeahead text, deterministic matching only - no model runs here.

workarea_id.description: With action suggest: optionally restrict to one granted vocabulary workarea.

curie.description: With action get or hierarchy: the term's CURIE. Unknown and out-of-scope are indistinguishable (fail closed).

direction.description: With action hierarchy: which way to look over ratified is_a, served from the per-release closure (a lookup, never a traversal).

release.description: With action hierarchy: optional release id; defaults to the owning vocabulary's latest ratified release.

term.description: With action mappings: the CURIE whose ratified mappings to return.

limit.description: Page size, where the action paginates (suggest, hierarchy, mappings).

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page.
